blogs.title: The Mootness Minefield: Lasting Litigation Rights When Overtime Gets Paid Up Front
blogs.description: An analysis of the Eighth Circuit's remand on the MFLSA claim, specifically focusing on the *Laidlaw* doctrine of 'good business practice' and the standing implications of voluntary cessation. This post explores the tension between a plaintiff recovering liquidated damages (private relief) and the state retaining rights to statutory penalties (public remedy), challenging practitioners to consider when a wage dispute becomes procedurally moot despite current monetary redress.

blogs.title: Legislative Intent as a Litigator: Reading Section 181.101 Through the Commissioner's Lens
blogs.description: A deep dive into the MPWA statutory interpretation used to deny Cohen's penalty claim. This post dissects the 8th Circuit's method of comparing Minn. Stat. § 181.101 to §§ 181.13 and 181.14 to discern that penalty collection is restricted to the Labor Commissioner. This provides legal scholars with a case study on how federal courts apply 'plain meaning' rules to determine state enforcement authority in federal district courts.

blogs.title: The Procedural Cost of Casual Claims: Why 'New Relief' Does Not Save a Summary Judgment Appeal
blogs.description: An examination of the Eighth Circuit's dismissal of the MWTA penalties and injunctive relief due to lack of preservation. This post highlights the critical importance of aligning summary judgment motions with appellate brief arguments, specifically analyzing the waiver consequence of failing to provide statutory authority for a request, and the court's refusal to consider shifting injunctive relief posture without a proper record.
